valuesSource: Each environment's infra/terraform/environments/<env>/terraform.tfvars, integration_alert_thresholds: the setting below without its IntegrationMonitoring:Policy prefix, ':' written '__', per integration code. This register names the thresholds; it holds no value, so a value is written in one place.
openQuestion: PTBC-037 (operational alert thresholds: availability, freshness, queue backlog, reconciliation mismatch), owner AHDA IT / DevOps Lead, gate Before Production (docs/governance/ptbc-themes.csv). PTBC-046 is cited with it by the workbook, but its subject is not recoverable from the sources (ptbc-tbc-tracker.md 9.5), so no threshold here is attributed to it. Until a threshold is CONFIRMED with a reference, PROD sets no value for it.

routing.recipients: The family's recipient roles and channels in the NOTIFICATION_ROUTING version in force (FG-04; WF-15 resolves them). Proposed: R01, in-app and e-mail, mandatory. TBC-INT-17 (recipients, escalation routes) is AHDA's.
routing.onCall: Every alert raised is also counted by the log-based metric <name_prefix>-operational-alerts-raised and sent to the on-call channel (ALERT_CHANNEL_WEBHOOK_URL) by the policy '<name_prefix> operational alert raised' (infra/terraform/monitoring/operations.tf), in SIT, UAT and PROD.
routing.windowBasis: The configured window: an alert reaches its recipients within 5 minutes of its threshold being crossed, the threshold TASK-091 set for the uptime alert (health-checks-uptime-monitoring.md D-7). PTBC-037 and TASK-093's response targets may set another.

stages.stage: FG-05's pass notices a time-driven breach (backlog, freshness, delivery rate, availability delay); a telemetry-driven one is raised as the attempt is recorded
The outbox dispatcher hands the committed intent to WF-15
WF-15 routes it: the in-app notification is stored SENT
WF-15 sends the e-mail on its next pass

thresholds.meaning: How long the integration stays DOWN (its latest technical outcome a failure) before the alert is raised. One alert per outage, even if an operator closes it while the outage goes on.
thresholds.withoutValue: Raised at once, on the technical failure that takes the integration DOWN (TASK-075 behaviour).

thresholds.meaning: How long after its last success the integration is still FRESH; the alert is raised when it goes STALE.
thresholds.withoutValue: Freshness stays UNKNOWN and no FRESHNESS alert is raised.

thresholds.meaning: The queue depth (attempts in flight plus operations awaiting a retry) beyond which the alert is raised; exceeded when the depth is greater than the value.
How long the oldest queued operation may have waited since its first attempt before the alert is raised.
thresholds.withoutValue: No QUEUE_BACKLOG alert on age. With AT-3 also set, either one raises the alert.

thresholds.meaning: How many mismatches a reconciliation may find without an alert; the run records every mismatch whatever the tolerance, and repairs none.
thresholds.withoutValue: Any mismatch raises the alert (TASK-075 behaviour).

thresholds.unit: rate, greater than 0 and at most 1
thresholds.meaning: The delivery rate over IntegrationMonitoring:Policy:MetricsWindow below which the alert is raised (built by TASK-075).
Raised when an operation is dead-lettered: every dead letter is an alert, one live per integration (TASK-075 D-9). No threshold: a dead letter is a final failure an operator must handle.
